note: Commands use the verbal noun (masdar), not the imperative; no capitalisation. Keep "…" when the English has it.
Instructions to the user use the singular imperative, as Arabic desktop software does; errors may use «يُرجى» + verbal noun.
Arabic comma, semicolon and question mark; quotation marks «…» around names; colon and parentheses as in English.
Western digits as in the source; units, ×, ° and keys unchanged; no space before %.

The paragraph direction follows the first strong letter: start a text with an Arabic word rather than a Latin one where natural. Where a text must start with a Latin word or a placeholder, it starts with U+200F (RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK); `import` adds it and `check` requires it.

Wrap a left-to-right fragment that contains punctuation (an extension, an option, a path, a number with its unit, a range, w × h, a config example) in U+2068 (FIRST STRONG ISOLATE) … U+2069 (POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE), or it is drawn as eop. or language--. Not around a single word or a placeholder standing alone (docs/translating.md, "Right-to-left languages").
